title: A Comparative Study of Deep Q-Networks and Traditional Algorithms for Multi-Agent Shortest-Path Search in Dynamic Graphs
description: This study compares prioritized breadth-first search, Dijkstra and A* with solo-trained and shared-policy deep Q-networks for navigation on static and changing unit-cost grids. Ten policies from five training seeds were frozen after static 5×5 training and evaluated without learning on 120 new geometries spanning 5×5, 10×10 and 15×15 sizes, one/two/four agents and two wall probabilities. The final protocol produced 15,120 unique evaluation episodes; three fresh timing rollouts per episode were not treated as extra outcome samples. Across all conditions, replanning A* completed 642/720 episodes (89.17%), shared DQN 799/3600 (22.19%), and solo DQN 870/3600 (24.17%). All recorded first trajectories passed replay auditing, and actual collisions were zero under the common rejection rules. Success-conditioned paths, matched comparisons and descriptive variation across model seeds are reported alongside failures. The findings apply to fixed small-map-trained policies and current-map prioritized planners under this protocol; they do not establish a universal algorithm ranking or a general reinforcement-learning adaptation advantage.
notes: Research preprint; not peer reviewed. Evaluates frozen static-small-map-trained policies under the stated protocol; results do not establish universal algorithm superiority.
